verb.example: We enjoyed walking along the beach at sunset.

noun.zh: 喜悅；快樂；令人高興的事
noun.example: The children shouted with joy when they saw the gifts.
Reading is a source of great enjoyment for her.
Her joyfulness brightened the whole room.

adj.zh: 歡樂的；令人喜悅的(主要形容場合或事件)
adj.example: The wedding was a joyous occasion for both families.

adj.zh: 快樂的；喜悅的(主要形容人的感覺)
adj.example: She gave a joyful laugh when she heard the news.
The long winter made the town seem cold and joyless.

adv.example: The students joyfully welcomed their new teacher.
He completed the task joylessly and in silence.

verb.example: I will accompany you to the train station.

noun.example: She enjoys the company of her close friends.
The dog became his faithful traveling companion.
Many older people value companionship and conversation.

adj.example: Each pack contains a book and accompanying CD.

verb.zh: 把……本質化；歸納為固定本質（專業用語）
verb.example: We should not essentialize an entire culture from one example.

noun.example: Trust is the essence of a strong friendship.

adj.example: Clean water is essential for good health.

adv.zh: 本質上；基本上；大體而言
adv.example: The two plans are essentially the same.

verb.example: The architect conceptualized the building as an open public space.

noun.example: The teacher explained the concept with a simple example.
Our conception of success changes as we grow older.
The diagram provides a clear conceptualization of the system.

adj.example: The course begins with a conceptual overview of the subject.

adj.zh: 構思的；形成概念的（少見）
adj.example: The activity develops students' conceptive abilities.

adv.example: The two theories are conceptually different.

adv.zh: 以構思方式；概念形成地（少見）
adv.example: The problem was approached conceptively before calculations began.

verb.example: The nation mourned the loss of a respected leader.

noun.example: The family observed a period of mourning.

adj.example: A mournful song played at the memorial service.

adj.zh: 沒有哀悼的；無悲傷的（罕見）
adj.example: The story imagines a mournless world without loss.

adv.example: The violin played mournfully in the final scene.
The characters moved on mournlessly in the strange tale.

noun.example: She felt deep sorrow after saying goodbye.

adj.example: He gave us a sorrowful look before leaving.

adv.example: She sorrowfully accepted that the journey was over.

noun.example: We bought a cake for the special occasion.

adj.example: There may be occasional delays during construction.

adv.example: We occasionally meet for lunch after work.

verb.example: The shared goal united the entire community.
The event reunited friends who had not met for years.

noun.example: The workers formed a union to protect their rights.
Our family reunion takes place every summer.

adj.example: The team remained united during the crisis.

verb.example: We anticipate a large crowd at the festival.

noun.example: The children waited in eager anticipation.

adj.example: The hospital took anticipatory measures before the storm.

verb.example: The train will arrive at noon.

noun.example: We celebrated the arrival of the new baby.

verb.example: The children decorated the classroom with paper flowers.

noun.example: The handmade decoration hung above the door.

adj.example: The bowl is decorative rather than practical.

verb.example: I prefer tea to coffee in the morning.

noun.example: Please tell us your seating preference.

adj.example: A quiet room would be preferable for the meeting.
Online payment is the preferred method for many customers.

adv.example: Please submit the form today, preferably before noon.

verb.example: Did you receive my email yesterday?

noun.example: A small reception was held after the ceremony.
The receptionist helped me make an appointment.

adj.zh: 樂於接受的；善於接納的
adj.example: The manager was receptive to our suggestions.

adv.example: The audience listened receptively to the new proposal.

verb.zh: 盡情享用；宴請；使大飽眼福
verb.example: We feasted on fresh seafood by the harbor.

noun.example: The family prepared a feast for the holiday.

verb.example: Clouds began to form over the mountains.
All products must conform to safety standards.
Too much heat can deform the plastic.
Please inform us of any change to your address.
The government plans to reform the education system.
The renovation transformed the old building.

noun.example: Please complete this form in black ink.
Scientists studied the formation of the island.
The dog's body conformation suits long-distance running.
The website provides useful travel information.
The new law introduced major tax reform.
The neighborhood has undergone a remarkable transformation.

noun.zh: 變壓器；促成轉變的人或事物
noun.example: The transformer reduces the voltage for household use.

adj.example: Travel was a formative experience in her youth.

adj.zh: 正式的；正規的；禮節性的
adj.example: A formal announcement will be made tomorrow.
We had an informal discussion over lunch.

adj.zh: 遵從的；符合規範的（少見）
adj.example: The design follows a conformative approach to industry rules.

adj.zh: 提供資訊的；增進知識的
adj.example: The guide gave an informative talk about local history.
Voters need reliable facts to make an informed choice.

adj.zh: 帶來重大轉變的；變革性的
adj.example: Education can be a transformative force in society.

adv.zh: 在形成或成長過程中（少見）
adv.example: The experience influenced her formatively during childhood.
The agreement was formally approved on Monday.
The group meets informally once a month.

verb.example: The new building resembles a sailing ship.

noun.example: There is a strong resemblance between the two sisters.

verb.example: More than fifty students participated in the competition.

noun.example: Active participation improves the learning experience.
Each participant received a certificate.

adv.zh: 以參與方式；共同參與地（少見）
adv.example: The plan was developed participatively with local residents.

verb.example: It is unkind to mock someone for making a mistake.

noun.example: His unfair trial was a mockery of justice.

adj.example: Students took a mock exam before the final test.

verb.example: I recognized her voice immediately.

noun.example: The scientist received international recognition for her work.

adj.example: The mountain is recognizable by its unusual shape.

adj.zh: 無法辨認的；面目全非的
adj.example: The town was almost unrecognizable after the rebuilding.

verb.example: She cycles to work whenever the weather is good.
Please recycle glass bottles and metal cans.

noun.example: The water cycle is powered by the sun.

adj.zh: 以自行車運送的；經循環處理的
adj.example: The cycled materials passed through the machine twice.
The bag is made from recycled plastic.
Most of the packaging is recyclable.

verb.example: The analyst annualized the quarterly growth rate.

adj.zh: 每年的；年度的；一年生的
adj.example: The school holds an annual music festival.

adv.example: The safety equipment is inspected annually.

verb.example: Please wait here until your name is called.
A difficult decision awaits the new manager.

noun.example: After an hour of waiting, the bus finally arrived.
The waiter brought us the menu.
The waitress recommended the soup of the day.

verb.example: The bird escaped through an open window.

noun.example: The hikers had a narrow escape from the falling rocks.
